speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn with yellowish skin; to determine the cause, is your baby feeding well and do they have any fever or lethargy?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-day-old male newborn. The newborn's mother reports that her child has developed yellowish discoloration of the skin that started from the face and then spread to the trunk since the past day. There have been no changes in his bowel habits or urination. The baby was born full-term at 38 weeks’ gestation via an uncomplicated vaginal delivery and has been exclusively breastfed every 2–3 hours.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Physiological Jaundice (Breastfeeding Jaundice). The onset after day 3, full term gestation, and lack of bilirubin elevation factors (like poor feeding or dehydration) strongly suggest physiological jaundice rather than pathological causes. I will monitor for any worsening signs and confirm with a bilirubin level if symptoms progress.
